headline: Ratchet & Clank's matched code becomes easier to navigate and maintain
summary: Contributors can work with named levels, buttons, hero states and shared structures instead of repeated numeric offsets and private declarations. All 5,116 functions still match the original game's bytes, with code holding at 100.00% and matched data at 73.94%; the compact progress report does not identify a release. The day's 231,369 added and 208,167 removed lines largely reflect formatting: #169 alone adds 169,328 and removes 147,550.
highlights: Data blocks and pointer references now build from C using values generated from contributors' own game images; retail values are not committed (#196, #197, #198).

New checks guard against matching regressions and track suspect compiler-dependent constructs; some constructs remain because removing them changes the compiled bytes (#194, #195, #200, #201, #202, #204).
Source folders and reference documentation were reorganized for contributors (#167, #191, #192, #210).
The level-extraction issue #165 was closed as completed.
